entries.title: Ezekiel 23:2
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Two women - Judah, and Israel, two kingdoms.

entries.title: Ezekiel 23:3
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Whoredoms - Idolatry.

entries.title: Ezekiel 23:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Aholah - That is, his own tabernacle; for Israel falling off from the house of David, fell off from the tabernacle, or temple of God; so that all the temple they had was of their own making. The elder - Greater for number of tribes, and for power, wealth, and for multitudes of people. Aholibah - That is, my tabernacle in her: the two tribes had the temple of God with them. Mine - By solemn marriage - covenant. Bare sons - Were fruitful and brought forth children to me; they increased in numbers of people; and among these, some there were that were children of God by faith, love, and obedience.

entries.title: Ezekiel 23:5
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Played the harlot - United in idolatry, with the Assyrians. Mine - When under my government, and protection.

entries.title: Ezekiel 23:6
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Horsemen - Skillful in riding, and well furnished with choice horses.

entries.title: Ezekiel 23:7
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: With all - Other nations, with whom she had commerce.

entries.title: Ezekiel 23:10
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Discovered - Stript her naked, and exposed her to shame. Took her sons - Captives. Slew her - The kingdom of Israel, under Hoshea, was by Salmanesar utterly destroyed. They - The Assyrians, had executed God's just displeasure upon her.

entries.title: Ezekiel 23:15
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Girded - With soldiers belts, which includes the rest of the habit of soldiers. In dyed attire - Both rich, comely, large, and of divers colours. Princes - Of princely aspect and majesty.

entries.title: Ezekiel 23:17
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Alienated - She grew weary of the Chaldeans.

entries.title: Ezekiel 23:18
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Discovered - Made it appear to all, far and near.

entries.title: Ezekiel 23:19
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: By - Remembering her idolatries in Egypt, her alliance with it in days past, which she now resolved to act over again.

entries.title: Ezekiel 23:20
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Paramours - The nations, that were confederate with the Egyptians.

entries.title: Ezekiel 23:23
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Pekod - Pekod is the province between Tigris, and Lycus; in this was old Nineveh. Shoa - Either Sia in Armenia, or the Sohia, among which were the Adiabeni, and this contained the middle part of the kingdom of Babylon. Koa - This bordered upon Media, the inhabitants were called Kohai, and dwelt about Arbela. And all - All subjects of the Assyrian monarchy.

entries.title: Ezekiel 23:24
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: And wheels - Lest in their march the carriage wheels should break, a store of these were provided. An assembly - A mighty confluence of people. I will set - Give them a power in right of conquest over their rebels, as well as mine, and I will give them a spirit of judgment to discern the greatness of this people's sins. Judge - Condemn, and execute sentence upon thee. According - To their will, power, wrath, and custom, against rebels; for these are their rules of judgment.

entries.title: Ezekiel 23:25
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: I will set my jealousy - As a jealous provoked husband, I will be as much against thee as they are. Thy residue - Either the people, who hid themselves in vaults and cellars, or what the Chaldeans cannot carry away, all this shall be devoured by fire.

entries.title: Ezekiel 23:29
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Take away - Deprive thee of the comfortable use of all thy labour, which they will exact of thee in captivity.

entries.title: Ezekiel 23:32
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: It - Is large, and contains what will last many years, even 'till the seventy years be expired.

entries.title: Ezekiel 23:34
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Thou - Shalt stagger with sorrows, that shall intoxicate, and astonish. Suck it out - The dregs shalt thou drink, and multiply thine own sorrows. Break the sheards - To suck out what remains. And pluck - Revenging thyself upon thyself.

entries.title: Ezekiel 23:35
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Bear thou - The guilt, I will impute it, the punishment, I will not pardon it.

entries.title: Ezekiel 23:38
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: In the same day - When they had newly polluted themselves with idolatry and murder, they thrust into the temple.

entries.title: Ezekiel 23:39
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: My house - Nay, these things have been in my house.

entries.title: Ezekiel 23:40
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Wash thyself - After the manner of harlots.

entries.title: Ezekiel 23:41
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Sattest - Prepared to feast them. A stately bed - A magnificent bed, on which women sat to feast, when men leaned on their sides. Incense - Offered to their idols.

entries.title: Ezekiel 23:42
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: A voice - A shout for joy, that there was a treaty of peace between the Jews, and the Chaldeans.

entries.title: Ezekiel 23:45
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Righteous men - Men that keep the law of their God.

entries.title: Ezekiel 23:46
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Upon them - Against the Jews, the children of this Aholibah.

entries.title: Ezekiel 23:47
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The company - The Babylonian army.

entries.title: Ezekiel 23:48
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Lewdness - Idolatry. And indeed we do not read of any after their return out of this captivity.

entries.title: Ezekiel 23:49
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: They - The Babylonians. The sins - The guilt of worshipping idols; and you shall bear the punishment of idolaters.
